title: Removable media carrying a signed DID
description:
A USB stick is plugged in. On it is a DID, signed by an authority. The signature is what makes it worth believing, and persona-08sz is where that authority was recorded.

NOTHING IN THE TREE DOES THIS. No udev, no mount watching, no USB handling anywhere. persona-lnaj proposes a FIXED drop directory; removable media is a transient mount at a path nobody knows in advance, which is the part lnaj does not model. did_key.rs reads the HIRE_DID_KEYS environment variable -- no file, no signature. persona-vmpi.2 is did:web, which anchors in DNS and HTTPS rather than in an enrolment signature.

SHIPPABLE IN THREE STAGES, EACH USEFUL ALONE. Do not wait for the last one.

  1. Scan mounted volumes for a well-known relative path and enumerate what is
     there. Produces a Candidate and nothing else. Needs no enrolment, no
     signature verification, no new trust model -- and is already useful,
     because some other attestor may be able to prove that identity. This is
     the model working as persona-lnaj describes, not a shortfall.
  2. Verify the signature against an authority enrolled per persona-08sz, and
     emit evidence. This is the step that mints a credential.
  3. Notice the unplug.

TIER IS CAPPED AT IAA2 AND THE REASON IS PHYSICAL, not a policy choice. Plain USB storage has no compute, so the private key must LEAVE the stick to sign. Possession of the stick is therefore not exclusive possession: anyone who copied it holds that identity permanently and the original owner cannot tell. So this is hardware-adjacent, not hardware-bound, and Iaa3 is unavailable however good the enrolment signature is. Say this in the doc comment, because the shape of the thing invites the opposite assumption.

PROOF COST IS SILENT. Reading a mounted filesystem and checking a signature interrupts nobody, so it declares ProofCost::Silent and is eligible for the unprompted path (persona-jl4j.3).

STAGE 3 IS MORE INTERESTING THAN IT LOOKS, AND WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS. Unplugging is an OBSERVED departure, the class persona-3tly.6 wants and currently has only two members of (PC/SC card removal, screen lock). But it is the weakest of the three: pulling a CAC removes the signing CAPABILITY, while pulling this removes only the copy you happened to be reading. Treat it as evidence the user left, not as evidence the identity became unusable.

Also worth knowing: mounting untrusted removable media is itself a filesystem attack surface, and the daemon does not get to choose when it appears. Read the well-known path and nothing else; do not walk the volume.
acceptance_criteria: Stage 1 alone, merged and useful: a mounted volume with the well-known file yields a Candidate, declared Iaa2-attainable and Silent, proving nothing. Stages 2 and 3 land separately.
